@graph.name: Trigger GitHub Workflow
@graph.description: System must allow triggering GitHub Actions workflows via API with custom inputs
@graph.rationale: Enable automated deployments and builds through ICA natural language commands
@graph.acceptanceCriteria: API accepts workflow_id, ref, and inputs parameters. Workflow triggers successfully on GitHub. Returns confirmation with timestamp and workflow details.

@graph.name: List Available Workflows
@graph.description: System must provide endpoint to list all available GitHub Actions workflows
@graph.rationale: Allow users to discover available workflows before triggering
@graph.acceptanceCriteria: Returns list of workflows with name, path, and state. Includes workflow metadata.

@graph.name: Get Workflow Run History
@graph.description: System must allow querying recent workflow runs with status and details
@graph.rationale: Enable monitoring of deployment and build history
@graph.acceptanceCriteria: Returns paginated list of runs. Includes status, conclusion, timestamps, and GitHub URLs.

@graph.name: API Response Time
@graph.description: API must respond within acceptable time limits

@graph.name: Service Availability
@graph.description: Service must be available when needed

@graph.name: API Key Authentication
@graph.description: All API endpoints must require valid API key for authentication

@graph.name: HTTPS Communication
@graph.description: All communication must use HTTPS encryption via ngrok tunnel

@graph.name: GitHub Token Security
@graph.description: GitHub personal access token must be stored securely in environment variables
@graph.threatMitigated: Token exposure and unauthorized repository access
